## 2026-09-17 V15.3.33 async/navigation performance pass
- Removed the unconditional `await Task.Yield()` at the start of section navigation; this removed roughly one UI frame (~18-21 ms in prior NAV_PHASE logs) from each section switch.
- Added a low-memory fast path in MemoryPressureService so navigation does not request GC memory-load data when working set is below the pressure threshold.
- Removed a redundant `Task.Run` wrapper around the already-async/cached Network Analyzer readback.
- Hardened unguarded async UI event handlers (main navigation, subsection navigation, Optimization Plan button and styled dialog action button) through SafeTaskService.Forget so exceptions are observed/logged instead of surfacing as unhandled async-event crashes.
- Deadlock audit: no `.Wait()`, `GetAwaiter().GetResult()` or explicit `async void` in active code; remaining async event handlers have local try/catch. The single `.Result` use is guarded by `IsCompletedSuccessfully`.
- Idle baseline stayed very low (~0.013% normalized CPU over 15 s; working set about +1 MB; no handle growth).
- Build profiling confirmed WinUI/XAML is the main compile cost: MarkupCompilePass2 ~6.5 s, CoreCompile ~2.55 s, XamlPreCompile ~2.09 s.

- QueueDirtyStateRefresh nyní vždy používá jediný dispatcher queue slot bez ohledu na thread; burst změn se coalescuje na max 1 UpdateDirtyState za dispatcher tick.
- Classic ToggleSwitch callback nyní používá QueueDirtyStateRefresh místo přímého UpdateDirtyState.
- Virtual TweakVirtualRowViewModel callback nyní používá QueueDirtyStateRefresh místo přímého UpdateDirtyState.
- ApplyClickCoreAsync a Discard_Click po RefreshCards používají QueueDirtyStateRefresh, takže nepřidávají další okamžitý full-scan.
- Přidán RunDirtyRefreshCoalescingSmokeAsync a full-smoke gate:
  - 1000 QueueDirtyStateRefresh požadavků musí vytvořit právě jeden pending dispatcher refresh,
  - po yield/drain se _dirtyRefreshQueued vrátí na 0.

## V15.4.62 — AI Remover TrustedInstaller heartbeat + bounded module timeouts
- Navázáno na V15.4.61.
- RemoveWindowsAI runtime hardening:
  - upstream holý $R.WaitForExit() je při runtime patchi nahrazen 15s polling smyčkou,
  - každých 15 s vypisuje "[Spanky] TrustedInstaller child still running... Ns" do stdout/progress konzole,
  - TrustedInstaller child hard timeout snížen z 480 s na 360 s,
  - při překročení limitu se child proces ukončí a vznikne jasná timeout výjimka.
- Per-module limity:
  - běžné AI moduly: 8 min,
  - Advanced RemoveCBSPackages / RemoveAIFiles: 15 min,
  - worker client má pouze +1 min rezervu nad per-module timeoutem místo původních 35 min,
  - ProcessRunner při timeout/cancel dál používá Kill(entireProcessTree: true), takže se ukončí celý worker/PowerShell strom.
- AI progress UI:
  - TimeoutException má vlastní stav "Timeout" místo obecné "Chyba",
  - progress konzole vypíše explicitní TIMEOUT řádek a informaci, že procesní strom byl ukončen,
  - OperationJournal ukládá stage TimedOut,
  - po timeoutu se další vybrané moduly mohou dál zpracovat.
- AI heartbeat UI pro dlouhé CBS/TrustedInstaller kroky zůstává aktivní.
- AI runtime hardening smoke aktualizován na nový model:
  - vyžaduje WaitForExit(15000),
  - vyžaduje TrustedInstaller heartbeat text,
  - vyžaduje timeout after 360s,
  - upstream holý $R.WaitForExit() nesmí v runtime skriptu zůstat,
  - hardened runtime musí projít PowerShell parserem.

## 2026-09-20 - V15.4.116 stale-cache + force-refresh race hardening
- InstalledAppService now protects inventory publication with an inventory generation. A stale summary/detail scan can no longer repopulate caches after force refresh, invalidation, or heavy-cache trim.
- InstalledAppService completion cleanup now clears _summaryFlight/_detailFlight only when the completing task is still the active flight, so an older completion cannot detach a newer scan.

## 2026-09-20 - V15.4.123 Winget status hardening + cache-residency audit
- Added --ui-cache-residency-smoke to measure steady-state memory held by full WinUI page caches across 18 representative sections.
- Cache residency audit result: populated ~250 MB WS / 191 MB private / 4 MB managed / 1517 handles; full UI cache trim freed only ~2 MB WS / 2 MB private / 2 MB managed / 2 handles. Rebuilding all 18 sections averaged 8.9 ms, max 32 ms (GPU), and rebounded ~25 MB private. Conclusion: aggressive global cache budget would not materially reduce RAM and would increase native/WinUI churn, so it was intentionally not introduced.

- Changed WingetUpdateService.GetStatusAsync to run winget --version and the upgrade scan sequentially, avoiding two simultaneous winget.exe instances.
- Hardened status correctness: failed winget --version now makes fresh status fail rather than reporting Available=true with an unknown version; failed winget upgrade scan now throws instead of returning an empty list that could falsely display 'all apps are current'.
- Added --winget-status-smoke: clears in-memory and persistent Winget status/cache, performs a fresh version + upgrade scan, requires Available=true and a non-empty/non-'nezn?m?' version.

- Added a versioned persistent Debloater logo map keyed by PackageFullName (installed-app-logo-map-v1, 7-day TTL). PackageFullName includes package version, so updated packages naturally miss stale entries.
- Every cached non-null logo path is validated with File.Exists before reuse. Missing paths fall back to ResolveLogo() and replace the stale entry; null logo results are also cached to avoid repeated directory enumeration.

- Added logo hit/miss instrumentation to InstalledAppService detail inventory logs.

- Background persisted-inventory refresh is now delayed 650 ms and starts only if Debloater is still the active section. Fast cross-section navigation therefore cancels the expensive worker scan before it starts.

Deferred Overview/GPU hydration is generation-bound so stale completions cannot repopulate UI state after invalidation.

## 2026-09-21 - V15.4.150 transaction safety, drift watchdog, hardened process runner, startup inventory V2
- Continued from V15.4.149 and integrated the high-value architecture ideas selected from pc-tweaker-app without changing the app's visual design.

- Hardened ProcessRunner for trusted Windows utilities: System32 resolution, restricted child PATH/PATHEXT/SystemRoot/WINDIR, PowerShell module path hardening, cmd.exe /D injection, and a PATH-poison smoke test.

## 2026-09-24 V15.4.272 - DNS physical-adapter targeting + MTU/DNS separation hardening
- Fixed DNS Apply/read-back target selection so WFP/LightWeight/filter/virtual/VPN/tunnel adapters are excluded.
- DNS now targets only active real adapters that have a usable IPv4 address and IPv4 default gateway; current machine resolves to `Ethernet / Realtek Gaming 2.5GbE Family Controller` with 192.168.1.108 and gateway 192.168.1.1.
- MTU adapter selection hardened with the same WFP/filter/virtual exclusions.
- MTU backend still never calls DNS apply code; added a DNS fingerprint invariant around MTU Apply so DNS is read before/after but never written.
- If DNS changes externally during an MTU operation, the MTU change is rolled back and the operation fails explicitly while DNS is left untouched.
- `MTU_APPLY_OK` now logs `dnsInvariant=unchanged` on verified success.

- Implemented the requested optimizer expansion except the two explicitly excluded blocks: **Process Optimization pro hry** and **Gaming Latency Optimizer**.

- Network A/B: Interrupt Moderation / Flow Control / Packet Coalescing / LSO are manual A/B tests only; A/B measures latency + jitter + loss, retains the test state only for a measurable improvement and automatically restores the original setting otherwise; RSC has the same A/B + rollback behavior.
- RX/TX buffer Latency / Balanced / Throughput presets are derived only from the actual driver's valid values; no guessed hard-coded buffer numbers. TCP Auto-Tuning is shown against Recommended=Normal.
- Removed duplicate WMI scans by carrying buffer valid-values in the existing NIC capability snapshot. NETWORK_ADVANCED_CAPABILITY improved from measured ~418-591 ms to ~149-225 ms in 3/3 green NIC UI runs.

- Interrupt / Device Latency: added read-only MSI/MSI-X and interrupt-affinity inventory for GPU, NIC, NVMe/storage and USB controllers; GPU/NVMe affinity is not rewritten automatically.
- Added an explicit NIC-only affinity A/B experiment using Spread messages across processors, persistent original-state backup, NIC restart, latency/jitter/loss comparison and automatic rollback on a non-improvement/failure; if a test state is retained, UI exposes **Vrátit původní NIC affinity** and blocks a second experiment until rollback is resolved.

## DEV 15.4.363 — reversible tweaks + cleaner scan + GPU compatibility + data-driven registry
- Implemented the Sparkle-inspired pieces as native .NET/WinUI architecture, without importing Electron/GPL source.
- Reversible tweak model formalized: TweakDefinition now exposes RevertAsync/CanRestoreOriginal/RevertMode; registry tweaks restore the exact original registry value through RegistryBackupStore, while ordinary boolean command tweaks remain reversible through SetAsync(previous). IOptimizerModule now exposes original-value restore and TweakEngine has an exclusive RestoreOriginalAsync path with verify/read-back + OperationJournal entries.
- Existing transactional apply/rollback/history infrastructure remains the core: atomic registry snapshot, write-ahead transaction, read-back verification, TweakBatchHistory per-batch undo and OperationJournal. The new original-value revert path complements rather than duplicates it.
- Data-driven tweak registry: CatalogService routing is now backed by TweakCatalogSource descriptors + indexed factories instead of a section switch. TweakBatchHistory resolver consumes the same registry, removing its duplicated hardcoded source list.
- Cleaner upgraded from one aggregate Temp-only scan to real category scanning: User Temp, Direct3D shader cache, NVIDIA DX/GL cache and AMD DxCache are measured independently and in parallel. Storage UI now shows measured MB per category with selectable checkboxes, cleans only selected categories, then rescans and reports actual freed/remaining bytes + failed locked files.
- Fixed old mismatch where the Storage cleaner text claimed shader caches but GetSafeCleanupSize/ClearSafeCaches only covered Temp; safe cleanup now genuinely includes all listed shader cache paths.
- GPU compatibility detection expanded to gpu:any / gpu:nvidia / gpu:amd / gpu:intel plus legacy nvidia/amd/intel scopes, with explicit detected-vendor reason text when unsupported. NVIDIA telemetry remains NVIDIA-scoped; Intel telemetry is now Intel-scoped instead of being offered on every machine.
- Driver-start tweaks were upgraded to exact original-value revert too, so every registry-backed tweak audited by the catalog now has original-value restore metadata.
- V14 audit smoke extended to gate the new architecture: data-driven registry size, original-value revert coverage for registry tweaks, NVIDIA/Intel scope metadata and Cleaner category/total consistency. First run correctly exposed 25 legacy driver tweaks missing original-value revert; fixed them, rerun passed.

## DEV 15.4.364 — Storage cold/warm backend optimization
- Storage temperature probe is now truly cold-lazy. If no fresh/stale persistent temperature snapshot exists, ReadStorage returns disk inventory immediately without waiting for MSFT_StorageReliabilityCounter, queues a background temperature refresh, then invalidates only the storage snapshot when the refresh completes so the next render picks up temperatures.
- Existing stale-while-revalidate path is preserved. Temperature mutation generation still prevents stale background writes; the dedicated stale-cache smoke now seeds its fresh baseline explicitly before testing preserve/stale/background-refresh behavior.
- Storage TRIM cache invalidation was separated from ordinary storage refresh. The existing 5-minute TRIM cache now survives normal inventory/PnP/temperature refreshes; it is explicitly invalidated only after real TRIM mutations from Storage Recommended or the storage.trim tweak.
- Measured storage backend improvement on target PC: previous cold STORAGE_NATIVE_PHASE example ~490 ms with temperaturesMs ~463 ms. New cold runs ~111–122 ms. Repeated/cache-invalidated warm storage reads now ~18–46 ms with trimMs=0 and temperaturesMs=0 after cache establishment.
- NIC Recommended fast-adapter change validated with real --nic-smoke: adapterMs dropped from prior ~59–192 ms examples to 11 ms; total profile 339 ms, remaining propertiesMs=264 ms is the intentional fresh advanced-property provider/read-back authority and was not unsafely cached.

## DEV 15.4.372 — Button reentrancy / focus-safe async actions
- Hardened QuickButton and StyledDialogButton against duplicate async activation with per-button Interlocked single-flight guards.
- Removed the previous IsEnabled=false busy behavior from both shared helpers after QA exposed a real keyboard hazard: disabling the focused button causes WinUI to move focus to the next control, so a rapid second Enter can trigger a neighboring action instead of being ignored.
- New contract: the active button stays enabled/focused, duplicate Click/Enter events are atomically discarded, and focus does not jump to a sibling action while work is running.

- Strengthened keyboard activation QA with deterministic TaskCompletionSource-held actions rather than timing-based Task.Delay actions. The smoke holds the first action open, injects another real Enter during execution, verifies count stays at 1 and focus remains on the same button, then releases the action and verifies the next activation succeeds.

## DEV 15.4.372 — Dynamic page scrolling / clipping hardening
- Visual size telemetry exposed a real production layout bug: PageScroll had VerticalScrollMode=Disabled globally even when PageHost was much taller than the viewport, making lower content unreachable.
- Added dynamic page scroll policy: hidden scrollbar is preserved, but VerticalScrollMode switches to Enabled only when PageHost.ActualHeight exceeds the viewport and returns to Disabled when the page fits.
- Scroll policy is refreshed on PageHost size changes, RootGrid size changes, redundant navigation and every successful section navigation.
- Replaced per-event Task.Delay settle work with one reusable 60 ms DispatcherTimer debounce, avoiding task/log churn during deferred layout growth and resize.
- Added queued+dirty coalescing so size changes that arrive while a policy refresh is already pending cannot be lost.
- Visual size QA now waits for a stable PageHost height and matching scroll policy over multiple samples instead of relying on a fixed delay.
- Size matrix now fails on scroll-policy mismatch and horizontal overflow, and logs viewport/PageHost/ContentStack/Scrollable metrics.
- Initial measurements found inaccessible overflow as large as 522 px on compact Overview, 339-366 px on Network and 860-964 px on Settings with scrolling disabled.
- Removed dead TopActions vertical space: TopActions is never populated in current code but permanently consumed 14 px. Its margin is now zero.
- Reduced normal PageHost bottom padding from 10 px to 8 px. Together with the dead-margin cleanup this removes the former ~16 px Overview micro-scroll at 1320x860 without shrinking cards or text.
- Final size matrix passes all 9 combinations (Overview/Network/Settings at 980x680, 1320x860, 1600x1000) with horizontal overflow=0.
- Final behavior: Overview 1320x860 and 1600x1000 => scroll Disabled; compact Overview 980x680 => Enabled only because content truly overflows; Network/Settings => Enabled only when needed.
- VISUAL_SIZE_AUDIT_OK ms=2905.2.
- Full runtime validation: BUILD-TEST 67832.5 ms, exit 0.
- Visual regression remains deterministic and green: 6/6 snapshots, changedPercent=0%, worst mean RGB delta=0.009.
- FAST no-change remains healthy: 108.1 ms.

## DEV 15.4.372 — Reserved-control page-scroll routing
- Extended page-scroll-input smoke with reserved-control coverage for TextBox and Slider on a long Settings page.
